# Explain DockLayouts cross-window vessel lifecycles

## Context

Cross-window object permanence is a defining DockLayouts capability, but the current guide gives only the ownership map and the Adoption guide gives only the render-target hook. The final `window/` package now separates participation, workspace sets, tear-out, conversion, embodiment, and parking.

## The Problem

Readers lack one explanatory path through pane → popup vessel → conversion/parking → reintegration. Generic multi-window documentation and the portability matrix do not explain DockLayouts' semantic ownership, SharedWorker identity, native-titlebar handoff, or failure/terminal behavior.

## The Architectural Reality

`window/{Participation,WorkspaceSet,TearOut,VesselConversion,VesselEmbodiment,VesselPark,DragTarget}.mjs`, Workspace hooks, main-thread window operations, and dock-blind drag coordination divide the choreography. The App worker retains semantic truth; render targets and physical windows are embodiments.

## The Fix

Create `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsWindows.md`: a story-led guide following a real pane through tear-out, cross-window participation, conversion/parking, disconnect, and reintegration, with links to the generic multi-window concepts and portability reference.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Window guide | ADR 0029 + current window package + host hooks | Explain one lifecycle across semantic and physical owners | Revalidate terminals after refactors | New guide | Real headed multi-window journey |
| Portability relationship | Generic multi-window guide + tear-out matrix | Explain concepts; link matrix as reference | Never duplicate platform rows | Same guide | Rendered links + receipt |

## Decision Record

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The guide clears the full guide-authoring bar: source/tool-grounded narrative, reader-owned benefits, lived maintainer voice, and at least one render-verified `flowchart TD`.
- [ ] The guide separates explanation from reference: no inlined API/schema/test catalog, and no ticket or PR ids in guide prose.
- [ ] The new source guide is registered in `learn/tree.json` and the SEO `PRIORITIES` input; generated sitemap/LLM outputs remain untouched.
- [ ] Current-source consistency, guide lint, tree lint, portal rendering, and an independent cross-family whole-guide review are recorded in the PR.
- [ ] A real headed journey covers vessel birth, same-pane continuity where promised, conversion/parking, disconnect/terminal handling, and reintegration.
- [ ] The guide distinguishes App-worker semantic state, main-thread window authority, render-target embodiment, and drag coordination.
- [ ] Platform portability facts link to the existing matrix instead of copying it.
- [ ] Failure and cleanup paths are included, not only the happy tear-out animation.

## Out of Scope

A platform matrix rewrite, Electron/browser API reference, or new tear-out behavior.

## Avoided Traps

Do not treat a popup as the state owner, promise same JS heap across unsupported worker topology, or conflate native-titlebar drag with in-document drag.

## Activation Gate

Do not author the guide while #17836 remains an active refactoring authority. At pickup, re-run Memory Core mining, read the current ADR 0029 and source/test surfaces named below, exercise the relevant live subsystem, and revalidate the proposed guide boundary. If the final API makes this split wrong, reshape this ticket before writing—do not preserve a stale outline.
